collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — HISTORY AND COLLECTIVE MEMORY (HIS-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Old stories, ruins and abandoned places, heirlooms, disputed records, festivals that changed, names on carvings, customs nobody can explain, and the things a people remembers together: some of it painful and handled gently, some of it gloriously silly.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an elder and a child aged 6-13)

collection.description: An elder asks children to climb off the stone with two carved handprints: tell what it means, or let them keep climbing.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Near the inland stream there's a flat stone with two handprints carved deep into its top, side by side, as if two people pressed their palms there at once. Children love climbing on it. (subject) has just come along and asked them, gently, to climb down. (friend) wants to know why.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "Long, long ago," (subject) says, "there were two peoples on this island who fought. For a very long time. Then one day, two of their leaders met here, and put their hands on this stone, and agreed that it was over." (friend) looks at the handprints. "Did it stay over?" (subject) nods. "It did. Not everything was mended. But it stayed over." (friend) puts (friend.his/her) hand next to the carved ones, very gently. (subject) lets (friend.him/her).

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) changes (subject.his/her) mind. "Actually," (subject.he/she) says, "I think they'd like children playing on it. That was the point." (friend) doesn't understand, but climbs back up. (subject) sits nearby and watches them play, with a look on (subject.his/her) face that (friend) doesn't understand either. Later, (friend) asks (friend.his/her) family about the stone, and gets the whole story.
